cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's accounting machine review October's receivables for HANGS Construction: the money customers owe the company.
First, it reads the aging: unpaid customer bills, by age. It ties to the books.
Next, October's payments. One customer's check, about $32,400, was never matched to its bill.
Retainage, money held back until a job is done, checks out. But a signed change order, $15,780 of extra work, was never billed.
A promised credit was never issued. One customer is over 90 days late.
The allowance, a reserve for bills that may go unpaid, is about $11,000 short. Three letters are drafted.
Last, it writes the workpapers and an unsigned memo for the controller, the head of accounting.

All done. It proposes four journal entries, corrections to the books worth about $65,700. Eight items stay open for a person to decide, and three letters and a call script are drafted. Nothing is posted or sent until the controller approves.
